How to Convert 2 Fluid Ounces to Milliliters Precisely

When measuring delicate liquid extracts, syrups, or spirits in pastry baking, changing 2 fluid ounces to milliliters requires an exact multiplier. Volume metrics in culinary arts rely on regional standards, but the universal conversion standard mandates multiplying the precise fluid ounce component by 29.5735. This yields exactly 59.15 mL for a standard 2 oz volume line.

The Mathematical Conversion Formula

The calculation converts fluid units directly into metric capacities through multiplication:

  • Total Metric Volume (mL) = Given Volume (fl oz) × 29.5735
  • 2 oz Conversion Logic = $2 \times 29.5735 = 59.15 \text{ mL}$

Frequently Asked Questions

Q1: How many mL is 2 oz of liquid?

A1: 2 fluid ounces of liquid is equal to exactly 59.15 milliliters. In general casual home baking, this is commonly rounded up to a clean 60 mL.

Q2: What fraction of a cup is 2 oz of liquid?

A2: A standard US customary cup contains exactly 8 fluid ounces. Therefore, 2 oz of liquid constitutes exactly 1/4 of a standard measuring cup.

Q3: Is a fluid ounce the same as a weight ounce?

A3: No. Fluid ounces (fl oz) measure volume (the space a liquid occupies), while dry ounces (oz) measure weight. For pure water, 2 fl oz weighs roughly 2 dry oz, but heavier liquids like honey or molasses will weigh much more.
